page_title: T-MAC: CPU Renaissance via Table Lookup for Low-Bit LLM Deployment on Edge

sources.entry: T-MAC: CPU Renaissance via Table Lookup for Low-Bit LLM Deployment on Edge - Replaces unpacking and multiplying low-bit weights with bit-sliced lookups, so a narrower weight costs less to apply.

summary.title: T-MAC: CPU Renaissance via Table Lookup for Low-Bit LLM Deployment on Edge
summary.one_liner: T-MAC runs low-bit weight-quantized LLMs on CPUs by replacing dequantization and multiplication with bit-wise lookup-table kernels, reaching up to 4x throughput over llama.cpp.
takeaways: Dequantizing low-bit weights before matmul adds large overhead; T-MAC performs mixed-precision GEMM directly via lookup tables.
T-MAC turns data-type-centric multiplication into bit-wise table lookups, removing multiplications and reducing additions.
Its LUT-based kernels scale linearly with weight bit-width.
Reported results: up to 4x throughput and 70% lower energy vs llama.cpp on low-bit Llama and BitNet models.
BitNet-b1.58-3B reaches about 30 tokens/s on one M2-Ultra core, 71 tokens/s on eight cores, and 11 tokens/s on Raspberry Pi 5; code is open source on GitHub.
summary.summary: The paper introduces T-MAC, a lookup-table-based method for efficient inference of weight-quantized (low-bit) LLMs on CPUs. It argues that existing systems lack native mixed-precision matrix multiplication and instead dequantize weights, which causes overhead; T-MAC performs mpGEMM directly through bit-wise table lookups. The authors evaluate on low-bit Llama and BitNet models, comparing against llama.cpp and reporting throughput and energy gains plus token rates on M2-Ultra and Raspberry Pi 5. The system is open-sourced by Microsoft.
